Commentary: Anshul Kamboj [8.0-0-60-0] is back into the attack
Anshul Kamboj to Shai Hope, 1 run, yorker length from round the wicket, flicked through backward square leg for just a single as Hope can't run quickly
Anshul Kamboj to Gudakesh Motie, 1 run, 134.7kph, full toss from over the wicket, Motie backs away to slash and outside-halves to deep backward point

Anshul Kamboj to Shai Hope, no ball, FOUR, Shai Hope gets to 150. A brilliant knock which could be a match winning one. Hope gives himself room and thumps it over mid-on for a boundary. To make matters worse, Kamboj has overstepped. Free-hit coming up
Anshul Kamboj to Shai Hope, FOUR, four more! Full toss outside off, Shai Hope slaps it away through the covers. Jadeja runs to his right in the deep but doesn't put in a dive
Anshul Kamboj to Shai Hope, 1 run, swung away to deep midwicket

Anshul Kamboj to Gudakesh Motie, FOUR, 133.9kph, short delivery from over the wicket, Motie moves leg-side to pull and top-edges it over the keeper's head. This is turning out to be a very expensive over

Anshul Kamboj to Gudakesh Motie, SIX, 22 runs off the over! That's a terrific hit from Motie. Banged in short, Motie clears his front leg, slightly crouches, takes his eyes off the ball but he connects superbly as he pulls hard to send it over deep backward square leg
Naman Dhir [5.0-0-26-1] is back into the attack
Just 7 needed off the last two overs.
Naman Dhir to Shai Hope, SIX, 95.7kph, full toss outside leg and Hope gets low to slog it over deep backward square leg. Scores level

Naman Dhir to Shai Hope, 1 run, 80.7kph, short of length outside off, Hope goes on the back foot to slap it down to long-off. West Indies win by 5 wickets and it's fittingly their captain who hits the winning runs. This is West Indies' highest successful run-chase in ODIs

Keemo Paul (1/2): [What was the chat there with Shai struggling a bit?] Well yeah, obviously when I was in the middle with Shai, the plan was just to try and keep the required runs under eight runs per over. So that was basically the plan, like you said, Shai was struggling a bit. So I knew I had to take a few chances. [What was the discussion in the dressing room knowing that Jewell was injured?] Well yeah, I mean coach spoke to us saying we were just trying to break the game down in phases. I mean we saw India batted in the last two games and chasing is always good on these wickets. So we always had the confidence. We backed ourselves and we got the job done tonight. So that's awesome.

Paul (2/2): [Appreciation for your captain?] Definitely, definitely. Shai, he's a modern-day legend, man. And the way he's batted this series is quite amazing. So yeah, definitely. [On his performance going forward] Well, for me it's just not to get complacent. I just want to take it as a stepping stone and contribute to the team whenever I get the opportunity. I just want to keep performing. I'm happy and yeah, just do my best always. [Your thoughts on your bowling?] Well, like it's from the past two games, we had our plans. We were just trying to hit that length as hard as possible, the top of the stump length. So that was basically the plan on these wickets. It's quite tough. So you got to bring your skills out, try to scramble seam the ball as much as possible. So that was my plan.

Hope (2/2): [On West Indies' record run chase and the overall ODI series] I think we played some really good cricket in patches. The batters were scoring some runs. That's what we really wanted to do. So yeah, we've been doing really well for the last two, three years where batters have been more consistent. We asked them to put big scores on the board. It's always difficult bowling in these conditions. We know India, more batter friendly. You got to bring your skills out and very, very, very small margins for error. So from a bowling standpoint, we learned a lot. I'm sure the guys are going to take this and hopefully we can get a lot better in the bowling side of things going forward. [On recovering in time for the upcoming shorter format] So hopefully, I got two days to turn things around, so hopefully I'm match ready.

Gill collects the trophy and joins his team-mates. They pose with the WINNERS board. India won the first two matches convincingly with their top three batters doing the bulk of the scoring. Today, they lost Gill and Kohli cheaply. Rohit stepped up and missed out on another ton by 8 runs, Ruturaj Gaikwad scored 57 after being dropped four times but it was KL Rahul's unbeaten 129 that powered India to 351. In reply, captain Shai Hope opened the innings today and batted till the end to take his team over the winning line with a magnificent 162*, stitching four 50+ stands. Three matches were played in different parts of the country but the pattern remained similar. Good batting wickets, high-scoring encounters, centurions for both teams and the chasing team emerging victorious. It's time to bring the curtains down on this ODI series. The action now shifts to the shortest format. The 5-match T20I series commences on Tuesday (October 6th) and we'll be bringing you all the action. Until then, goodbye...
